title: Spot the variable with no ceiling, before the solve

blocks.text: A hospital's supply team keeps a purchasing model in MathOpt: order quantities, storage limits, supplier rebates and credits, some of them continuous with no upper bound. After a refactor the model came back `UNBOUNDED` in production, and the team wants a check that runs *before* the solve and names the variables that could be to blame.
A variable can make a feasible model unbounded on its own when three things hold together:

items: the objective rewards moving it one way (up for a positive coefficient in a maximization, down for a negative one; the reverse in a minimization);
it has no bound on that side (`upper_bound` or `lower_bound` is infinite);

no row stops it going that way. A row $`\ell \le \sum_j a_j x_j \le u`$ stops $`x_j`$ from growing when $`a_j > 0`$ and $`u`$ is finite, or $`a_j < 0`$ and $`\ell`$ is finite; it stops $`x_j`$ from falling in the two mirror cases.

blocks.text: Write `free_to_grow(model)` returning the sorted names of every variable for which all three hold. Useful calls: `model.objective.is_maximize`, `model.objective.get_linear_coefficient(v)`, `model.variables()`, `model.linear_constraints()`, and for a row `row.terms()` (each term has `.variable` and `.coefficient`) and `row.lower_bound`, `row.upper_bound` (infinite when absent).

This check is a cheap first look: a variable it names makes any feasible model unbounded, but a model can be unbounded along a direction that moves several variables at once, which it does not see. The tests build small models and compare the names. About twenty lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from growth import free_to_grow

m = mathopt.Model()
nurses = m.add_variable(lb=0, ub=25, name="nurses")
grant = m.add_variable(lb=0, name="grant")
overtime = m.add_variable(lb=0, name="overtime")
loan = m.add_variable(lb=-10, ub=float("inf"), name="loan")
m.add_linear_constraint(overtime - nurses <= 30, name="overtime_cap")
m.maximize(4 * nurses + 2 * grant + overtime - loan)

print("free to grow:", free_to_grow(m))
grant.upper_bound = 500
print("with grant capped at 500:", free_to_grow(m))
m.minimize(4 * nurses + 2 * grant + overtime - loan)
print("same terms, minimized:", free_to_grow(m))

cases.says: a variable the objective rewards, with no upper bound and in no row, is named; one with an upper bound is not
a row stops a variable only on the side its bound faces, given the sign of the variable's coefficient
a minimization pushes a variable the opposite way from a maximization
a variable with no lower bound can run away downward

concepts: a variable pushed by the objective, with no bound or row against it on that side, runs away
